I am 64 years old and have worked this land in Quzhou County for 40 years. I never went to school, but I know this soil and this climate with my own two hands. My farm is 8.5 mu, and there are only two of us in the household now — my wife and me. Our main cropping system is wheat-maize, same as every family around here. That rotation is reliable; the grain station buys both crops, and I know exactly when to sow and harvest without reading any book.

I also keep a cotton plot — about 2 mu. Cotton brings decent money when the price is right, and I have grown it for many years. But at my age, with only the two of us, I cannot manage too much cotton. It needs many sprays and must be picked by hand. So I keep 2 mu of cotton and put the remaining 6.5 mu into the wheat-maize rotation.

It is now spring, and my winter wheat is already in the ground from last October. I will top-dress it with urea at green-up and again at jointing. I will pump water from my well four times — the overwintering irrigation, green-up, jointing, and heading. I will spray twice for aphids and yellow rust. After wheat harvest in June, I will plant summer maize directly into the stubble without tilling — there is no time to waste in the summer heat, and the soil is still soft. I will use hybrid seed, apply fertilizer at planting and side-dress at the big-bell stage, and irrigate twice if the summer rain is not enough. For cotton, I will rotary-till the 2 mu plot in April, sow the improved guoxinmian seed I know, apply compound fertilizer and urea, irrigate three times through the season, and spray for pests about eight times. I will pick the cotton by hand in autumn.

I do not experiment with new crops or fancy methods. I follow what my father taught me, what my neighbors do, and what this land has always given me.
